history.summary: DUPLICATE/OVERLAP: this temple is already documented in the dataset as file 2287.json, id 'gnana-saraswathi-temple-basara' ('Sri Gnana Saraswathi Temple (Basara)'). Research notes: one of India's very few temples where Saraswati is the presiding deity, on the banks of the Godavari at Basara. Legend: after the Kurukshetra war, Maharishi Vyasa settled in this Dandakaranya spot and made sand murtis of Saraswati, Lakshmi and Kali; the place was called Vasara, later Basara. Traditionally built in the 6th century by Bijialudu, a Karnataka king ruling Nandagiri (Nanded); idols were reinstated in the 17th century by a Nandagiri chieftain after destruction by Muslim invaders (per Wikipedia). The goddess sits holding a veena; Lakshmi stands beside her in the sanctum and Mahakali is on the first floor - Basara is considered the abode of the divine trinity. Famous for the Akshara Abhyasam ritual (formal induction of children into education). CSV town 'Adilabad' corrected: actual town is Basara (census town, Nirmal district). CSV state 'Adilabad' corrected: Telangana.

name: Basara Saraswati Temple
town_description: Basara (also spelled Basar) is a census town in Nirmal district, Telangana, on the banks of the Godavari near its confluence belt with the Manjira, about 205-210 km from Hyderabad and 70 km from Nirmal. It is a major pilgrimage town centered on the Gnana Saraswathi temple, with an own railway station (Basar, BSX) about 2.4 km away.

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (about 210 km)
travel.railway: Basar (BSX), about 2.4 km; Nizamabad about 34.8 km
travel.road: Well connected by TSRTC/MSRTC buses; Hyderabad about 205-210 km, Nizamabad about 34.8 km, Bhainsa about 30 km

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Vasantha Panchami (January-February) is the peak for Akshara Abhyasam
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:00 AM - 12:30 PM, 2:00 PM - 8:30 PM (Telangana Endowments Department)
